images.title: Sevenths beat eighths
images.purpose: Show that with the same top number 4, sevenths give a bigger share than eighths, so 4/7 is more than 4/8, which is one half.
images.composition: Two upright chikki bars standing side by side on one baseline with wide space between them, and one comparison line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: one upright rectangular chikki bar cut across into 7 equal pieces; the bottom 4 pieces filled teal #0072B2, the top 3 plain. Right: one upright bar of exactly the same height and width, standing on the same baseline, cut across into 8 equal pieces; the bottom 4 pieces filled amber #E69F00, the top 4 plain. One thin dashed reddish purple #CC79A7 horizontal line runs across both bars at the top of the teal shading, showing the teal reaches higher. Centred below: one comparison line. Exactly 2 bars, 15 pieces, 4 teal, 4 amber.

images.takeaway: Same number of pieces, but sevenths are bigger, so 4/7 is more than 4/8.
images.description: Two same-size upright chikki bars, one in 7 equal pieces with 4 teal and one in 8 equal pieces with 4 amber; the teal reaches higher, so 4/7 > 4/8 = 1/2.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say why 4 sevenths stand taller than 4 eighths when both bars are the same size.

image_decisions.why: Equal counts of bigger and smaller pieces side by side make the same-numerator comparison visible.
